VETERANS AFFAIRS COMMISSION MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 8, 2025
  6335 MYRTLE AVE., LONG BEACH

Juanita Doplemore, Chair  Victor Hill, Commissioner
Kenneth Osborn, Vice Chair  James Schotter, Commissioner
Antawnette Atkins Blade, Commissioner  Nicholas Sramek, Commissioner
James Goodin, Commissioner

  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Osborn called meeting to order at 4:43 p.m.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter

Commissioners Absent: Hill

Also present: Erica Valencia-Adachi, Collective Impact Manager, Gina Overholt, Coordinator.

Also in attendance: Christina Boatwright, John Oppenheim, Rachele Ross, Brian Skieff, Ryan Antes,
Sylvia Contreras, Alex De Leon, Councilmember Roberto Uranga, Jesse Soria, Alison King,
Alexandria O’Bard, David Espinosa, Henry Schotter, Mayor Rex Richardson, Jeff Williams, and
Anaya Rivera.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Chair Osborn lead the Pledge of Allegiance. Pledge of Allegiance followed by Staff Report. Staff
liaison (Overholt), reported that a muster event organized by Selected Marine Corps Reserve will take
place on Saturday, February 8, at the Hilton Long Beach. The OVS connected the organizer with VA
Long Beach contacts.Commissioner Sramek asked about whether more funds may be obtained for
the Veterans banners program. Commissioner Goodin suggested the OVS look into a neighborhood
program grant.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  25-54032  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Veterans Affairs Commission
  meeting of Wednesday, December 11, 2024.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Doplemore, seconded by
  Commissioner Schotter, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by
  the following vote:

  Yes:  6 Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0 None

2.  25-54033  Recommendation to approve draft nomination form for Veterans Banner Program.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Doplemore, seconded by
  Commissioner Sramek, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by
  the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hill

  The Commission reviewed and discussed the draft nomination form for the
  Veterans banners program. Suggestions were made to improve the form by
  including the historic Armory on 7th Street in the list of military-related places in
  Long Beach to which prospective nominees should have a connection. Also, less
  than 10 alternative nominations from last year may be considered for this year’s
  program.(They were not selected because of the limited number of
  banners).Nominees who did not provide complete applications or usable photos will
  be invited to submit applications for this year. The banners selection subcommittee
  will continue to meet to discuss the media release, selection criteria, nomination
  evaluation form, outreach activities to promote the program and garner a diverse
  pool of nominees, and more.

3.  25-54034  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on Veterans Banner Program
  outreach activities and banner locations.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Sramek, seconded by Commissioner
  Doplemore, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hill

  Veterans banners subcommittee chair Osborn asked the Commission to identify
  potential locations for banners in detail by the end of January. The suggested

PUBLIC COMMENT

John Oppenheim, founder and CEO of the Long Beach Area Veterans Collaborative, spoke about the
holiday donation drive sponsored by Councilmember Kerr’s office in partnership with the
Collaborative. The drive, which collected many items at several small business and other CD 5
locations between Veterans Day and December 27, was very successful. The items were sorted and
stored at the Health Department’s Public Health Emergency Management warehouse. Items from the
donation drive were delivered to Century Villages at Cabrillo today, where they will be distributed to
Veterans in need. Oppenheim encouraged collaboration on future donation drives.
 Rachele Ross, Financial Aid Specialist with the Long Beach City College Veteran Services Office,
announced the Veterans Health Fair on March 27, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. in the A quad of LBCC’s
Liberal Arts Campus. She invited the Commission to reach out to any organizations that may be
interested in participating, as well as to help promote the event.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Staff liaison (Overholt) announced the upcoming 2025 Long Beach Point In Time (PIT) Homeless
Count on January 23, and encouraged Commissioners to volunteer by going to the volunteer
registration website.

ADJOURNMENT

Chair Osborn adjourned the meeting at 5:26 p.m. A well-attended holiday celebration followed with
elected officials, leaders of local Veterans organizations and more in attendance.
